comparison: Perfect alignment on brain volumetric findings (C46-C47, C51-C53). Both evaluations support the claims about genotype and treatment effects on brain volumes, with longitudinal measurements showing transient vs. persistent effects. Both rate these claims as SUPPORTED.

Strong alignment on background claims about DS and Ts65Dn model (C1, C5-C7, C9-C11, C14, C17-C18, C23-C27). Both evaluations recognize these as well-supported literature-based claims providing essential context. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

High overlap on RNAseq findings (C86-C93). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, noting appropriate interpretation of minimal DEGs with citations. Peer review rates as UNCERTAIN, noting methodological concerns about RNAseq approach and lack of explicit acceptance of the interpretation that minimal gene expression changes can produce phenotypic effects.

Strong alignment on neurodevelopmental testing claims (C54-C62). Both evaluations support the multivariate and univariate statistical evidence, including maternal care controls. Both rate as SUPPORTED with recognition of rigorous longitudinal assessment.

Strong alignment on main treatment conclusions (C3-C4, C30-C32, C35-C37, C98-C101). Both evaluations support the negative findings showing GTE-EGCG treatment did not provide therapeutic benefit and exacerbated certain phenotypes. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Strong alignment on MRS metabolite findings (C79-C85). Both evaluations support the hippocampal metabolite data showing genotype and treatment effects. Both rate as SUPPORTED as part of the comprehensive multi-system assessment.
Strong alignment on prior literature about GTE-EGCG effects (C12-C13, C15-C16, C19-C22, C28). Both evaluations recognize these as appropriately cited literature review claims. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Strong alignment on cognitive testing data (C63, C69-C78). Both evaluations support the comprehensive cognitive assessment across two timepoints showing genotype and treatment effects. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Moderate alignment on craniofacial and brain phenotyping (C2, C29, C33-C34, C38, C48-C50, C95-C96). Both evaluations support the imaging evidence. Peer review also includes cognitive (C57-C58, C64-C68), metabolite (C79, C81), RNAseq (C88), and drift (C97) claims in their evaluation, showing broader grouping. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Both address methodological generalizability (C106). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting the claim is speculative about future applications without direct evidence. Peer review rates as SUPPORTED, affirming the methodology is solid but requesting a priori power calculations, suggesting methodological details need clarification.

Alignment on pharmacokinetic literature claims (C102-C104). OpenEval groups these with dosing rationale (C105) as methodological details. Peer review groups them with other literature claims. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Partial overlap on bone phenotyping. OpenEval R5 addresses BMD and tibia microarchitecture (C39-C45), noting limited genotype effects. Peer R2 includes some bone claims (C39-C40, C44-C45) within broader treatment effects evaluation. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Minimal overlap on tibia microarchitecture (C41). OpenEval R5 provides detailed evaluation of bone findings including limitations. Peer R8 briefly acknowledges tibia findings as part of comprehensive multi-system assessment. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Minimal overlap on bone phenotyping (C42-C43). OpenEval R5 specifically notes mild and non-significant genotype effects on tibia. Peer R1 includes these claims in broader phenotyping evaluation. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Both address genetic drift claim (C97). OpenEval R9 provides detailed evaluation with convergent evidence from multiple phenotypes. Peer R1 includes drift acknowledgment within broader phenotyping evaluation. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Both address dosing rationale (C105). OpenEval R12 groups this with pharmacokinetic literature as methodological details rated SUPPORTED. Peer R11 includes it with methodology evaluation rated SUPPORTED but notes need for power calculations.

Minimal overlap on integrative interpretation (C94). OpenEval R6 notes this claim links metabolite, volumetric, and cognitive data as part of SUPPORTED MRS evaluation. Peer R7 groups it with RNAseq findings rated UNCERTAIN due to methodological concerns.
